name: Al Gore
role: US vice president (1993–2001), Democratic presidential nominee (2000) and climate campaigner
summary: A Tennessee Democrat who moved from a moderate record in Congress to a mainstream liberal platform as vice president, favoring expanded health coverage, targeted tax cuts, abortion rights and gun checks alongside free trade with labor and environmental standards. Since 2001 he has focused on climate change, urging a global emissions cap, a carbon tax and clean electricity, and has criticized executive overreach and surveillance.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2000 acceptance speech he promised to move toward universal health coverage step by step, starting with all children; his plans expanded coverage through public programs and subsidies rather than a single government-run system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pledged to raise the minimum wage so that work always pays more than welfare, and in 1999 proposed adding $1 to it; the size of the increase was modest rather than dramatic.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In his Nobel lecture he urged a cap-and-trade treaty because emissions trading uses the market to allocate resources efficiently, and he has called capitalism the system he would keep; he also favors strong regulation, so the evidence is mixed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: A 1991 Senate speech called for shifting the tax burden from middle- and lower-income families toward the richest, citing the top 1 percent's falling share of taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Backing the 1992 striker-replacement bill, he told the Senate it mattered not only for organized labor but as a measure of equity for the whole society; campaigning in 2000 he said he was pro-union and pro-organized labor.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Promised to stand up to polluters, HMOs, tobacco and drug companies and backed an enforceable Patients' Bill of Rights; in 2000 he described his regulatory style as smaller government but stronger regulations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Supported the 1996 welfare overhaul with time limits and work requirements and said he wanted to move people from welfare to work, while also pushing a higher minimum wage and tax credits; he did not call for cutting benefits as such.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Said the terror threat is real and backed surveillance under the FISA court process he voted for, but denounced warrantless domestic surveillance as unlawful, so his view depends on judicial oversight.

legalize-drugs.rationale: His 2000 platform called for a national crusade against drugs, tougher drug policies and drug testing of prisoners and loosening of rules only for medical marijuana under strict supervision.

strong-leader.rationale: Argued in 2006 that a president who bypasses Congress and the courts threatens the constitutional design, warning that unchecked executive power endangers liberty.

state-harmful.rationale: Campaigned on making government work for people and defended Social Security, Medicare and public schools; he warned against big government but treated the state as necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Backed mandatory background checks, child safety locks, photo licensing for handgun owners and an assault-weapons ban while saying he supported the right of hunters and law-abiding citizens to own firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proposed 50,000 more community police and promised the best-equipped armed forces; he opposed expanded executive powers beyond legal checks.

rehabilitation.rationale: In 1992 he backed both military-style boot camps and drug treatment prisons for offenders, a mixed record that points both ways on rehabilitation versus punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: His 2000 acceptance speech defines family values broadly (honoring parents, caring for the sick, child care); no primary source found where he ranks traditional family structures as the foundation of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In a January 2008 Current TV video he said gay men and women ought to have the same rights as heterosexuals to make contracts, have hospital visiting rights and join together in marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said in his acceptance speech that he would protect and defend a woman's right to choose and opposed a Supreme Court that overturns Roe v. Wade.

more-religion-public.rationale: No primary source located: his 1999 Salvation Army speech on faith-based groups was only reachable through blocked archives, and the 2000 interviews searched do not address a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Pledged to defend affirmative action, enforce civil rights laws and end racial profiling.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In the March 2000 Los Angeles debate he said the country should allow more immigrants to come in, calling America a nation of immigrants and noting he had supported the 1986 amnesty.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Argued for treaties negotiated through the UN, said the US should pay its UN dues and favored UN treaties as a means to help poorer countries.

free-trade.rationale: Said "we must welcome and promote truly free trade" if it is also fair, and in the 1993 debate argued that lowering tariffs creates jobs and prosperity.

nation-first.rationale: Said America should not turn inward and called for strengthened partnerships and a new security agenda to avoid isolation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In the 2000 debates he said the US should get involved where there is genocide, as in Bosnia and Kosovo, and faulted Bush for standards under which genocide or ethnic cleansing alone would not justify using force.

limit-growth.rationale: In Senate speeches he said economic development must be sustained and in places accelerated, with technology reconciling it with the environment, and that a healthy economy and a healthy environment go hand in hand.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His Nobel lecture called climate change a planetary emergency requiring mobilization on the scale of wartime, a universal emissions cap and a carbon tax.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 2000 he favored renewable energy instead of nuclear power, but in 2025 said waste can be stored safely and predicted some resurgence of nuclear power while noting its cost.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In the 1993 debate he argued against raising tariffs, citing Smoot-Hawley, and later said protectionism only protects us from prosperity.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backed federal funding for strategic technologies such as robotics, biotechnology, and national computer networks, and proposed an energy trust fund directing investment toward renewables.

democracy-best.rationale: Conceded the 2000 election despite disagreeing with the court, and in his books argued for restoring the health of American democracy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Asked in 2000 about Lieberman's religious appeals, he said he and Lieberman feel strongly about the separation of church and state; he also spoke of his own faith on the campaign trail.

military-superiority.rationale: Pledged to keep America's defenses strong and its forces the best-equipped and best-trained in the world.

ethnic-nation.rationale: In March 2000 he called America a nation of immigrants and proud of it, saying all Americans except Native Americans came from somewhere else and that this made it a great nation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Wrote in 1994 that key escrow encryption offers a very effective way to serve national goals and defended it for phone networks.

results-over-ideology.rationale: In February 2000 he said he had always rejected both the liberal and conservative labels as out of date, and that as theory collides with reality one finds better solutions and should change views.

school-vouchers.rationale: Said in his acceptance speech he would not go along with any plan to give taxpayer money to private schools through vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Pledged to balance the budget every year and pay off the national debt, and said in 1999 he favored balance or surplus except in crises.

force-without-un.rationale: He defended the 1999 Kosovo campaign, waged without a Security Council mandate, and kept a nation's right to act against imminent threats; but in 2004 he faulted Bush for not honoring the UN and international law over Iraq, so the record is mixed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In his acceptance speech he said he fought for welfare reform to help people in trouble but to insist on work and responsibility, praising time limits and the move from welfare to work.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Voted for the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday and to override the veto of the Civil Rights Restoration Act, and campaigned on enforcing civil rights laws.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposed drilling in ANWR and offshore, and proposed ending dependence on carbon fuels and a moratorium on new coal plants without carbon capture.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He spoke of integrating immigrants through job training, education and health care (2000), which does not say whether they should give up their original culture; no primary source found on that.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His platform assigned government roles in health care, education, retirement security and environmental protection well beyond defense, justice and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said his campaign would honor the ideal of equality by standing up for civil rights, equal pay and equal rights for all Americans.

separated-powers.rationale: His 2006 speech defended checks and balances and warned that an executive claiming power to ignore Congress and the courts endangers the system.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He called diversity and inclusion a challenge that defines the nation (2000) but no primary source states a view on whether diversity makes society less cohesive.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Argued that following the rule of law makes the US safer and condemned warrantless surveillance and torture, allowing only a narrow inherent power against sudden immediate threats.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said the freedom of the Internet must be protected against government encroachment and control by media conglomerates.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said America must defend its interests from Europe to Japan and Korea, praised the building of NATO, required allies before using force, and called a Balkans troop withdrawal a damaging blow to NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Said in 2000, "I do support capital punishment, and I have always supported it," while saying a record like Illinois's would justify a moratorium and opposing a federal one.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: His position on abstinence and comprehensive sex education comes from an AP questionnaire reported by OnTheIssues; the original could not be found, so no evidence.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Only secondhand reports (OnTheIssues citing a press release and The Economist) say he supported debt relief; no speech or statement in his own words was found.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: No primary source found for his remarks on China or Malaysia (Anwar Ibrahim); the reports cited earlier were compilations.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In an April 1992 Senate speech he called for a global Marshall plan combining large-scale, long-term financial aid to developing nations with technology transfer, shared by the industrial nations.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Said in 2012 and 2016 that the president should be elected by popular vote and the Electoral College eliminated.

collective-defense.rationale: In 2000 he said America must defend its enduring interests from Europe to Japan and Korea and warned that withdrawing US troops from the Balkans would deal a damaging blow to NATO and jeopardize fragile alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In January 1991 he backed UN Security Council demands that Iraqi forces leave Kuwait, which he treated as an invasion to be reversed rather than a settled annexation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Argued in 2006 that a president who ignores legislative directives threatens a government of laws and not of men.

space-expansion.rationale: He backed the space station and NASA funding as a senator (1991), but his remark that a Mars mission should wait came only via OnTheIssues; nothing found on space expansion as a goal of civilization.

ban-cartels.rationale: He said in 2000 that if competition is valuable, as he thinks it is, antitrust laws embody the country's values, and as a senator he fought the cable monopoly because without competition there is no market.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Negotiated NAFTA labor and environment side agreements and said trade must come with binding standards on child labor, worker exploitation and pollution.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Said "mend it, don't end it" on affirmative action, promised in his acceptance speech to defend it, and rejected numerical quotas.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Pledged to pass the Employment Non-Discrimination Act and enforce all civil rights laws.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: His 2006 speech defended the Constitution and Bill of Rights as limits on executive power that should not be eroded by ordinary politics.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Described his decision to run for office as a refusal to turn away from service at home, as he had not turned from service in Vietnam.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His 1992 call for a global Marshall plan of long-term financial aid and technology transfer to developing nations contradicts relying on a poor country's own resources alone.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: In January 2000 he said the Confederate battle flag divides America, is a hurtful symbol recalling slavery, and should be removed from the South Carolina capitol and any government institution.

filial-duty.rationale: Said family values means honoring our fathers and mothers and caring for the sick.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Said he would not go along with a plan to privatize part of Social Security and called privatization stock market roulette, while offering voluntary supplemental accounts.

single-official-language.rationale: His statement opposing English-only laws comes from an AP questionnaire known only through OnTheIssues; the original was not found.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: In the October 2000 debate he pledged robust support to the groups trying to overthrow Saddam Hussein, and in 1991 he urged removing the Baathist regime as a policy goal; he did not specify arms.

corporate-influence.rationale: Promised to get all special-interest money out of politics and made campaign finance reform his first bill; he later wrote that money overshadows knowledge in democracy.

non-intervention.rationale: He said in the 2000 debates that genocide such as in Bosnia and Kosovo warrants US involvement and defended the NATO action in Kosovo, rejecting any absolute bar on intervention.

public-access-to-information.rationale: On Freedom of Information Day in 1986 he said that of all the rights Americans cherish, the right to know is among the most important.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: In the first 2000 debate he called for more public and charter school choice, while opposing vouchers that send public money to private schools, so he backs only part of a mixed-provider model.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In a 1986 Senate speech on Kurt Waldheim he called the record of Nazi activities during the Holocaust staggering and an unexplainable atrocity, treating its historical reality as settled.

assisted-dying.rationale: In 2000 he said states should have discretion on assisted suicide; his reported personal opposition comes only from Senator Wyden's account via OnTheIssues, which is not his own words.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He said in 2000 that he had always rejected both labels as out of date, and in 2019 that left and right labels are way out of date, asking whether solving the climate crisis is progressive or conservative.

social-market-economy.rationale: Credited the private sector as the engine of growth while pledging Social Security, Medicare, a minimum wage and regulation of polluters and HMOs.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pledged to keep the armed forces the best-equipped and best-trained in the world.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Advocated active alliances such as NATO and said America should avoid isolation.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Argued that government must act through laws enacted by Congress and applied by courts, not by executive decree.

online-participation.rationale: Argued in The Assault on Reason that the Internet can revitalize democracy, and his 2000 campaign ran the first online primary.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wrote that too much wealth in too few hands disrupts social stability and corrupts the incentives of capitalism, and called inequality out of control in 2013.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Asked in the January 2000 Democratic debate whether his Joint Chiefs would have to support allowing gays in the military, he said he would make support for his policy a requirement for appointment.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: In 1986 Senate speeches on homelessness he said local governments and charities alone cannot meet the need and that the problem is too big to cure by turning to local charities.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: His Nobel lecture called climate change a threat to the survival of civilization and urged urgent action.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Assault on Reason passage calling a good-versus-evil worldview a Christian heresy could not be checked in the original; his 2004 speech says there is good and evil in every person but does not address politics as such.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Said in his acceptance speech that the real values in life are spiritual, including faith and family, duty and honor.

gm-crops.rationale: In 1989 he told the Senate to push forward carefully on crop strains engineered for pest, disease and drought resistance, and in 2000 said GM crops that are safe and raise productivity should be usable, judged by sound science.

dense-cities.rationale: His smart-growth remarks (2000) are about letting local communities control sprawl; no primary source compares the environmental merit of cities and suburbs.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He voted for the 1991 Gulf War to reverse the invasion of Kuwait and, in the 2000 debates, backed using force against genocide in Bosnia and Kosovo, uses that go beyond defending the US against attack.

free-public-college.rationale: He proposed making college tuition tax-deductible and more Pell grants (2000), which neither endorses nor rejects tuition-free public college.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Repeatedly urged a carbon tax to shift taxes from employment to pollution, saying "we should tax what we burn, not what we earn."

future-generations.rationale: His Nobel lecture framed the climate response as a duty to the next generation, who will ask why the present one did not act.

arms-reduction.rationale: He specialized in arms control in Congress, urged meaningful arms control talks during the nuclear freeze debate (1982), and in 2000 pursued negotiated cuts while pledging to keep the military the strongest in the world.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He introduced the 1989 Employment Incentives Act and the 1991 Gore-Downey bill to expand the earned income tax credit for the working poor, and in 2000 promised an expanded EITC for the bottom fifth of earners.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Said environmental impact should be counted in measuring profit and criticized GDP for ignoring carbon costs.

farm-price-support.rationale: In the October 2000 debate he called the Freedom to Farm law mostly a failure amid low prices and promised to restore a meaningful safety net for farmers; he did not specify guaranteed prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: In 1989 he criticized simplistic demands for immediate unilateral disarmament, and in May 2000 said nuclear unilateralism would hinder rather than help arms control.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: He was an original cosponsor of the 1984 Armed Career Criminal Act and in 2000 said three-strikes penalties should be reviewed to focus on truly violent crime.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: His 2000 platform pledged civil rights enforcement, a hate crimes law and an end to racial profiling, treating discrimination as a continuing obstacle.

police-more-powers.rationale: Proposed 50,000 more community police and promised the best-equipped armed forces; he opposed expanded executive powers beyond legal checks. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

notes: His positions shifted over time: in the 1980s he opposed federal abortion funding and described homosexuality as wrong, and in 2000 he supported civil unions but not marriage; by 2008 he backed same-sex marriage. He opposed nuclear power in 2000 but spoke more favorably in 2025. His medical-marijuana statements in 2000 varied. Answers use his most recent clear statements. Deepening pass (claude-haiku-5-5, 2026-11-01): nulled inferences were already cleared (30 Oct). Added stated answers from Stanford Congressional Record speeches. Searched without finding stated positions: estate tax, precautionary principle, population, Electoral College, term limits, international criminal courts, pornography, China, Israel, Soviet and EU themes, Penan land rights (Sarawak), Nobel lecture points (page refused access, 403). Re-sourcing pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-01): restored answers the previous pass nulled for resting only on OnTheIssues or Wikipedia, each now cited to Gore's own words (2000 debate transcripts, CNN transcripts via MediaSum, Senate and House floor speeches); positions found only in compilations stay null. Searched without a primary source: debt relief, faith-based groups, English-only, assisted suicide, sex education, China and Malaysia, Mars, the "Christian heresy" passage of The Assault on Reason. The algore2000.com speeches archive (Wayback Machine) blocked requests and was not used.
